content:
Apple today released operating system updates containing a large number of security fixes; from the published technical details, it is evident that progress in the field of vulnerability research by artificial intelligence tools has been extremely rapid. Details are as follows.

AI tools credited in Apple's updates

Apple released earlier today:

  • iOS 26.6
  • iPadOS 26.6
  • macOS Tahoe 26.6
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8
  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8
  • tvOS 26.6
  • visionOS 26.6
  • watchOS 26.6

Following the release of the updates, Apple promptly updated its security advisories page, providing more detailed information on multiple fixed issues, including the affected components and devices, potential impact, Apple's remediation approach, and the list of researchers credited.

One notable point in today's documentation is that it is quite lengthy, particularly given that Apple released the 26.5.2 update less than a month ago, stating that it already included fixes originally scheduled for the 26.6 update cycle.

Another notable detail is that Anthropic researchers and Claude were credited in fixes related to WebKit, WebKit Storage, and WebDAV, with some results achieved in collaboration with Calif.io researchers.

The same research team stated in May this year that, using Anthropic's Mythos Preview model, they built a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit in just five days, targeting the M5 chip.

Within each operating system update released today, Calif had multiple core security fixes credited, involving approximately ten researchers, indicating that multiple teams independently reported the same underlying issue.

In fact, Apple's current update cycle also fixed numerous other kernel vulnerabilities; today's operating system updates collectively list 30 distinct CVEs.

It is worth mentioning that Apple has had access to Claude Mythos Preview since April this year through Anthropic's "Project Glasswing" programme. Therefore, the number of vulnerabilities discovered internally via Claude may exceed what is reflected in the public credit list.

Finally, Anthropic is not the only AI company appearing in this update's acknowledgements. Apple also credited work from OpenAI Codex Security, Z.AI's GLM, and NVIDIA's AI Red Team, among others.

Although some names appeared in last month's security update notes, today's update further demonstrates the pace of development in AI-assisted security research, and also reflects that companies must accelerate adjustments to their update schedules and bug bounty programmes to adapt to this new landscape.
